arxiv-2011-12502.title: New insights into temperature-dependent ice properties and their effect on ice shell convection for icy ocean worlds Journal: Earth and Planetary Science Letters
arxiv-2011-12502.creator: Evan Carnahan, Natalie S. Wolfenbarger, Jacob S. Jordan, Marc A. Hesse
arxiv-2011-12502.description: Abstract Ice shell dynamics are an important control on the habitability of icy ocean worlds. Here we present a systematic study evaluating the effect of temperature-dependent material properties on these dynamics. We review the published thermal conductivity data for ice, which demonstrates that the most commonly used conductivity model in planetary science represents a lower bound.

arxiv-2102-08467.title: ϵ \epsilon -Arithmetics for Real Vectors and Linear Processing of Real Vector-Valued Signals with Real Vector-Valued Coefficients
arxiv-2102-08467.creator: Xiang-Gen Xia
arxiv-2102-08467.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a new concept, namely ϵ \epsilon -arithmetics, for real vectors of any fixed dimension. The basic idea is to use vectors of rational values (called rational vectors) to approximate vectors of real values of the same dimension within ϵ \epsilon range.

arxiv-2210-04407.title: Probing Formation of Double Neutron Star Binaries around 1mHz with LISA
arxiv-2210-04407.creator: Lucy O. McNeill, Naoki Seto
arxiv-2210-04407.description: Abstract We propose a novel method to examine whether Galactic double neutron star binaries are formed in the LISA band. In our method, we assign an effective time fraction τ \tau to each double neutron star binary detected by LISA.

arxiv-2402-03085.title: Designing topology and fractionalization in narrow gap semiconductor films via electrostatic engineering
arxiv-2402-03085.creator: Tixuan Tan, Aidan P. Reddy, Liang Fu, Trithep Devakul
arxiv-2402-03085.description: Abstract We show that topological flat minibands can be engineered in a class of narrow gap semiconductor films using only an external electrostatic superlattice potential. We demonstrate that, for realistic material parameters, these bands are capable of hosting correlated topological phases such as integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states and composite Fermi liquid phases at zero magnetic field.

arxiv-2505-10102.title: Nonlocal Generalized Aw-Rascle-Zhang model: well-posedness and singular limit
arxiv-2505-10102.creator: Elio Marconi, Laura V. Spinolo
arxiv-2505-10102.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Elio Marconi, Laura V. Spinolo. We discuss a nonlocal version of the Generalized Aw-Rascle-Zhang model, a second-order vehicular traffic model where the empty road velocity is a Lagrangian marker governed by a transport equation. The evolution of the car density is described by a continuity equation where the drivers’ velocity depends on both the empty road velocity and the convolution of the car density with an anisotropic kernel. We establish existence and uniqueness results.

arxiv-2508-04894.title: Adversarial Attacks and Defenses on Graph-aware Large Language Models (LLMs)
arxiv-2508-04894.creator: Iyiola E. Olatunji, Franziska Boenisch, Jing Xu, Adam Dziedzic
arxiv-2508-04894.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated with graph-structured data for tasks like node classification, a domain traditionally dominated by Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). While this integration leverages rich relational information to improve task performance, their robustness against adversarial attacks remains unexplored.

arxiv-2509-10678.title: T2Bs: Text-to-Character Blendshapes via Video Generation
arxiv-2509-10678.creator: Jiahao Luo, Chaoyang Wang, Michael Vasilkovsky, Vladislav Shakhrai, Peiye Zhuang, Sergey Tulyakov, Peter Wonka, Hsin-Ying Lee, James Davis, Jian Wang
arxiv-2509-10678.description: Abstract We present T2Bs, a framework for generating high-quality, animatable character head morphable models from text by combining static text-to-3D generation with video diffusion. Text-to-3D models produce detailed static geometry but lack motion synthesis, while video diffusion models generate motion with temporal and multi-view geometric inconsistencies.

arxiv-2602-06080.title: The Riemann Ξ \Xi -function from primitive Markovian cycles II: Strip rigidity and divisor identification
arxiv-2602-06080.creator: Douglas F. Watson
arxiv-2602-06080.description: Abstract . We compare the Riemann Ξ \Xi –function to a canonical real-entire reference family arising from the cycle Laplacian developed in Paper I ( [ 4 ] ). These spectral determinants have only real zeros by self-adjointness. Our main tool is a rigidity lemma for holomorphic functions on horizontal strips.

arxiv-2602-23548.title: The Continuous p-Dispersion Problem in Three Dimensions
arxiv-2602-23548.creator: Sanjay Manoj, Melkior Ornik
arxiv-2602-23548.description: Abstract Abstract: The Continuous p-Dispersion Problem (CpDP) with boundary constraints asks for the placement of a fixed number of points in a compact subset of Euclidean space such that the minimum distance between any two points, as well as the points and the boundary of this compact set is maximized.

arxiv-2604-21816.creator: Anuj Sadani, Deepak Kumar

pmc-11438071.title: CD16+ as predictive marker for early relapse in aggressive B-NHL/DLBCL patients
pmc-11438071.creator: Sylvia Zöphel, Nadja Küchler, Johanna Jansky, Cora Hoxha, Gertrud Schäfer, Julius J. Weise, Joanne Vialle, Lea Kaschek, Gebhard Stopper, Hermann Eichler, Daniela Yildiz, Alina Moter, Philipp Wendel, Evelyn Ullrich, Claudia Schormann, Torben Rixecker, Onur Cetin, Frank Neumann, Patrick Orth, Moritz B
pmc-11438071.description: Assessing the prognosis of patients with aggressive non-Hodgkin B cell lymphoma mainly relies on a clinical risk score (IPI). Standard first-line therapies are based on a chemo-immunotherapy with rituximab, which mediates CD16-dependent antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). We phenotypically and functionally analyzed blood samples from 46 patients focusing on CD16+ NK cells, CD16+ T cells and CD16+ monocytes.

pmc-11555613.title: Clustering Based on Laboratory Data in Patients With Heart Failure Admitted to the Intensive Care Unit
pmc-11555613.creator: Sepehr Nemati, Babak Mohammadi, Zahra Hooshanginezhad
pmc-11555613.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a common condition that imposes a significant burden on healthcare systems. We aimed to identify subgroups of patients with heart failure admitted to the ICU using routinely measured laboratory biomarkers.MethodsA large dataset (N = 1176) of patients with heart failure admitted to the ICU at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, USA, between June 1, 2001, and October 31, 2012, was analyzed. We clustered patients to identify laboratory phenotypes.

pmc-11676703.title: Mass Spectrometry Imaging Reveals Spatial Metabolic Alterations and Salidroside’s Effects in Diabetic Encephalopathy
pmc-11676703.creator: Shuohan Cheng, Xianyue Meng, Zixuan Wang, Tianfang Lan, Zhi Zhou, Zhonghua Wang, Zeper Abliz
pmc-11676703.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Diabetic encephalopathy (DE) is a neurological complication of diabetes marked by cognitive decline and complex metabolic disturbances. Salidroside (SAL), a natural compound with antioxidant and neuroprotective properties, has shown promise in alleviating diabetic complications. Exploring the spatial metabolic reprogramming in DE and elucidating SAL’s metabolic effects are critical for deepening our understanding of its pathogenesis and developing effective therapeutic strategies.

pmc-12508599.title: Seroprevalence and associated risk factors of epizootic hemorrhagic disease virus in cattle from the northern region of Peru: first serological report
pmc-12508599.creator: Kevin PONCE, Jessica JURADO, Mercy RAMIREZ, Luis VARGAS-ROCHA, Dennis A NAVARRO-MAMANI
pmc-12508599.description: Epizootic hemorrhagic disease virus (EHDV) is a vector-borne pathogen that affects both wild and domestic ruminants. Climate influences vector-borne diseases by driving vector migration to new areas, where they spread the virus. However, the lack of surveillance in some areas hinders accurate assessment the true disease burden.

pmc-12617217.title: OA2300. Perceived well-being and safety in Urban Green Spaces: Case study from Crete
pmc-12617217.creator: I Christoforidi, D Kollaros, A Psaroudaki, M Papadakaki
pmc-12617217.description: BackgroundUrbanization has significantly changed the way people interact with nature and Urban Green Spaces (UGS) provide a vital opportunity for citizens to engage with the natural environment. Addressing citizens’ perceptions could enhance the effectiveness of greening strategies, a consideration of particular importance for islands in the Mediterranean basin given their unique characteristics.

pmc-13346327.title: Repeated aluminum ingestion alters human intestinal structure: focus on advanced 3D tissue models
pmc-13346327.creator: Giulia De Negri Atanasio, Lorenzo Dondero, Francesca Tardanico, Giorgia Allaria, Erica Lertora, Giacomo Rosa, Chiara Barisione, Caterina Ivaldo, Francesca Rispo, Tommaso Filippini, Ilaria Demori, Sara Ferrando, Maria Cristina Gagliani, Katia Cortese, Mario Passalacqua, Jan Markus, Silvia Letasiova,
pmc-13346327.description: Aluminum (Al³⁺) is a widespread environmental metal with potential effects on the intestinal epithelium. In this study, we evaluated the impact of dietary concentrations of aluminum on barrier integrity, histological organization, and gene expression in a 3D human intestinal tissue model.

pmc-13435298.title: Risk of Bias Associated with Varying Sampling Strategies for External Comparator Cohorts for Single‐Arm Trials: Insights from Aggressive Lymphoma
pmc-13435298.creator: Mikkel Runason Simonsen, Shiva Leisner, Ahmed Ludvigsen Al‐Mashhadi, Laurids Østergaard Poulsen, Matthew Maurer, Lasse Hjort Jakobsen, Tarec Christoffer El‐Galaly
pmc-13435298.description: Marketing authorizations for oncology drugs are often based on single‐arm trials (SATs), and real‐world data‐based external comparator cohorts (ECCs) are increasingly explored to contextualize results. In retrospective studies, comparators may be identified by time of diagnosis but included based on time of relapse; such sampling strategies can introduce bias, potentially leading to erroneous efficacy conclusions.
